## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `72a6ac398e8bacc5fc5bd81e1aac5bebdfa964eb`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md + scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs, scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs

Read at 2026-11-16T04:23Z. First review of this head; claim: comment 6907177684; lane request 6907150872 on mailbox #33873 (the lane's at-tier reviewer was unavailable). Independence: implemented in an os-steve project thread, dispatched by domain:skills#2 (os-steve); reviewed by os-tesla, who neither dispatched nor implemented it.

Card #34013 carries `security`, so this record stays at the rule layer; the detail behind M1 and S1 is handed to the seat privately and is not written here.

### ① Derived judgments

- The diff against the merge base `babda9d3` is the three claimed files, +181/-30, and matches the claim's file surface (6906299967). The merge `72a6ac39` has parents `2b9b4832` and main `43dd5656`; main changed none of the three paths between the merge base and `43dd5656`, and the combined diff of the merge is empty on all three, so the merge brought nothing into them.
- Reader, as built: `claimThreadSession` accepts one spelling (the key starting the line, one backticked session id in the signature's session shape, only blanks after it) and reads null for everything else, two key lines included. This agrees with the template line's key and value spelling in `SKILL.md` line 314. Confirmed in the code and in the battery's nine refused spellings.
- Roster join, as built: `claimDelegate` uses the existing claim, yield, release and signature readers, with no second parser. It lists the thread for an open card's newest unyielded claim that no `Release:` answers, under the seat that claim's first-line signature names. A released claim, a superseded claim and a closed card drop it. Confirmed.
- Fail closed on the claimed paths: `claims` not an array, a thread not an array, a card whose thread is not held whole, and a truncated `pm:dispatched` listing each make the roster unreadable and the H72 signature row NOT MEASURED. Omitting `claims` lists no card thread. Confirmed in code and pins.
- Not confirmed: the claim that the new source stands inside the same trust statement as the two older ones. See M1.
- Not confirmed at this head: the PR body's first Tests bullet ("the template carries exactly one `Thread session:` line and the reader reads its spelling"). Commit `2b9b4832` removed that read; see S2.
- CI on this head when read: 54 check-runs, 29 success, 23 skipped, 2 still running (`Test Core (1/8)`, `Live half-state sweep`), none failed. The verdict below does not depend on them.

### ② Semver level

None. PM tooling and one skill-template line; no package, no changeset (`skip-changeset`). `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right. New export: `claimThreadSession`; `H72_ROSTER_LISTINGS` gains a `claims` key; `h72RosterListings` and `seatSessionRoster` each take one more optional input and keep their old reading when it is omitted (for `h72RosterListings`, an omitted thread map reads unreadable as soon as one `pm:dispatched` card is open, which is the fail-closed side).

### ③ Boundary flags

- Tier S is right: the one governed path is `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md`; `scripts/pm/**` is not a `hits` path on the rules face.
- This PR is security-touching: it widens which sessions a seat's roster lists for the mailbox signature reading.
- `SKILL.md` stays at 329 lines (ceiling 329): one line added in the claim template, one deleted under 报告契约. The deleted line restated the `out_of_scope_findings` shape, whose home is `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` rule 3 (lines 53 and 54 carry `class:` + `reach:` + evidence or `carrier:`, and the "none of these" case). It is the second copy the line above it forbids, and it is not a security-discipline line. Agreed with the seat's L1 read.
- The new template line does not duplicate or contradict `seat-post-protocol.md`, `project-forms.md` 〈信箱 PR〉 or `untrusted-text.md` line 16: none of them lists the roster's sources, and `--mailbox-keys` stays the one printed form of the rule.

### ④ Design judgment

M1 (must-fix) — The roster's third source is not held to the author rule that the seat ruling (6899217687) names as the fleet's outer defence. The `seatSessionRoster` docblock now states that all of the bodies it reads are written only by the relay. That holds for the two older sources and is not established for a card's comment thread, and no reader on the new path reads a row's author. A roster that a `listed` reading stands inside must be the fleet's own word in all three sources. Fix: apply the existing author rule (`MAILBOX_KNOCK_AUTHORS`) to the claim thread's rows before the join, with a row that names no author listing nobody; correct the docblock; pin it in both directions, for a listing and for each way a listing is dropped. New on this head.

S1 (should-fix) — The claim listing's NOT MEASURED covers the whole signature row and can be standing, not one sweep long. The threads are cache-only, and the code shows two populations of open `pm:dispatched` cards whose thread is never held whole at H72's point in the sweep. The PR body describes one of them as lasting "for that sweep". The summary also names no card, so a seat cannot find which one to repair. Fix: name the card numbers in the gap, state both populations in the banner, and either order the join after the thread is walked or say plainly that the row stays unjudged while such a card is open. New on this head. It lands with M1 or as its own card; the seat decides.

S2 (should-fix) — Nothing at this head binds the `SKILL.md` template line to the reader. Commit `2b9b4832` replaced the pin that read the template with a constant spelled inside the test, so the template and the reader can now drift with every check green, and the PR body still describes the removed pin. The same self-test already reads governed rule text for this purpose (`references/contract-review.md` and `references/project-forms.md`), so the stated reason does not set this read apart. Fix: restore a pin that reads line 314 (exactly one key line, the backticked placeholder directly after the key), and have `dispatch-gates` derive that read if the census is the obstacle; correct the PR body either way. New on this head.

N1 (nit) — The template line carries a parenthetical tail after the value, and the reader refuses any tail. A claim that keeps part of the note reads null with no write-time signal (the dev's Acceptance note on `post-stamped.mjs` names the carrier). Consider saying "nothing after the id" in the note itself.

N2 (nit) — Lifetime is pinned for released, superseded and closed. It is neither pinned nor stated for a reopened card whose old claim was never released, for a seat whose post is no longer held while its claimed cards stay open, and for age (a claim does not lapse by time). State each in the `claimDelegate` docblock as intended or not.

N3 (nit) — Stale wording: the `h72RosterListings` docblock still opens with "The two listings", and `knockSignature`'s "lists no session" reason names two sources.

N4 (nit) — The open question (must the claim signer's own session be listed) is answered A by the dev and the seat. A is consistent with the seat ruling, but the seat's stated reason ("already listed through its seat post") is not something the code checks. Record A as "the signer's session is not compared" in the docblock.

Does the change hold against the code it cites? The spelling, the join and the claimed fail-closed paths do. The trust statement for the new source does not (M1), so the control is not yet what the PR body says it is.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ef43bcaf3a6a4edc8bbcfb53ccda63644b33964a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md + scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs, scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs, scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.data.mjs

Delta review of this head against FAIL 6907259431 at 72a6ac39; claim: comment 6907865857; hand-off 6907767140 and lane request 6907772388 on mailbox #33873 (the lane's at-tier reviewer was unavailable). Independence: implemented in an os-steve project thread, dispatched by domain:skills#2 (os-steve); reviewed by os-tesla, who neither dispatched nor implemented it.

Card #34013 carries `security`, so this record stays at the rule layer; the detail behind each status below is handed to the seat privately and is not written here.

### ① Derived judgments

What moved since `72a6ac39`: one fix commit, `837f3acc`, and the merge `ef43bcaf` (parents `837f3acc` and main `31eb2aed`). Main changed none of the four paths between the two merged main heads, and the merge's combined diff is empty on all four, so the delta on the reviewed surface is the fix commit alone. The diff against main is four files, +311/-87: the three of the earlier head plus `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.data.mjs`, which the fix order allowed and the PR body names.

Status of each finding of record 6907259431:

- Prior M1: closed. `claimDelegate` now reads a card's thread under the knock's own author rule before any other reader runs: the rows are filtered with `recordAuthorTrusted` over `MAILBOX_KNOCK_AUTHORS`, the same predicate and the same list `readMailboxComment` uses, and no second list exists. The claim, yield and release readers all run on the filtered rows, so a row outside the rule, or one naming no author, lists nobody and neither supersedes, yields nor releases a claim. The `seatSessionRoster` docblock now states the trust root per source and no longer says every body is relay-written. Pinned both ways in three new battery rows: a relay claim and a `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` claim list; four shapes of other or absent author list nobody; an outside row leaves a relay claim listed against a newer claim, a release and a yield. The card's own claims are relay-authored, so the rule does not drop genuine claims.
- Prior S1: closed. The H72 block now runs after the dispatch-liveness loop, whose first statement walks every open `pm:dispatched` card, so both populations named in round 1 are held by then at no added request. A thread counts as whole only when that walk says so. `h72RosterListings` returns the unheld card numbers, `h72RosterReason` prints them in the NOT MEASURED reason, and the banner and the PR body say plainly that the walk's own residue keeps the signature half unjudged on every sweep while such a card is open. That standing residue is the part round 1 allowed to be stated instead of removed; see N1.
- Prior S2: closed. The battery again reads `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md`: exactly one line reads as the key, the backticked placeholder sits directly after it, the note says nothing follows the id, the bare spelling with a real id reads, and the whole template line with a real id reads null. The read is declared on the `self-test-reads` line and has its `GOVERNED_READ_FLOOR` row; `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` is green on this head. The PR body's Tests section now describes the pin that exists.
- Prior N1: closed. The template note says "nothing after the id" (`SKILL.md` line 314), and the pin above holds it.
- Prior N2: closed. The `claimDelegate` docblock states each lifetime case as intended: no lapse by age, a reopened card whose newest claim was never released lists again, the seat's post is not consulted.
- Prior N3: closed. The `h72RosterListings` docblock no longer says two listings, and `knockSignature`'s "lists no session" reason names the third source; the one existing row that spelled that reason was updated to match, a forced edit the PR body declares.
- Prior N4: closed. The docblock records that the signer's session is not compared.

Confirmed in the code at this head: the fail-closed paths of round 1 still hold (claims not an array, a thread not an array, a card not held whole, a truncated `pm:dispatched` listing each read the roster unreadable); omitting `claims` still lists no card thread. The PR body's counts agree with the source where read: the delegate battery has 17 rows against a floor of 17, the H72 battery 42 against a floor of 39.

### ② Semver level

None. PM tooling and one skill-template line; no package, no changeset (`skip-changeset`). `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right. Against main the exported surface is: `claimThreadSession` (new); `h72RosterReason` (new, added in this delta); `H72_ROSTER_LISTINGS` gains a `claims` key; `h72RosterListings` takes one more optional input and returns one more key, `unheld`, which the roster does not read; `seatSessionRoster` takes one more optional listing and keeps its earlier reading when it is omitted; `GOVERNED_READ_FLOOR` gains one row.

CI on this head when read: 54 check-runs, all completed, 32 success, 22 skipped, none running, none failed. `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Live half-state sweep` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are among the successes. The seat need not wait on any check.
CI completed before posting: 54 check-runs on this head, 32 success, 22 skipped, none failed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Tier S is still right: the one governed path is `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md`; `scripts/pm/**` is not a `hits` path on the rules face. The record carries no machine line for the low-risk skills arm because no changed path sits under a low-risk row.
- The PR touches security behaviour: it widens which sessions a seat's roster lists for the mailbox signature reading, and this delta narrows who may write the new source.
- `SKILL.md` stays at 329 lines (ceiling 329). The delta changes one line in it, the template note; the line paid for in round 1 is unchanged and was agreed there.
- The author rule is imported, not restated: no login is typed in the diff, and the printed `--mailbox-keys` line now says a claim counts only from an author the knock fence trusts. It does not contradict `seat-post-protocol.md`, `project-forms.md` 〈信箱 PR〉 or `untrusted-text.md`.
- Moving the H72 block changes when its findings are pushed, not what they are: nothing between the old and the new position reads an H72 finding or a mailbox counter, and no early exit sits between them.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

N1 (nit) — continues prior S1. The standing unjudged state that remains is stated and names its cards, but the reason does not say which cause holds a card (a walk at its page ceiling, or a failed page), and a truncated `pm:dispatched` listing shows only as the generic claim-threads gap with no card number. One open card can still hold the whole signature half unjudged for every mailbox; whether that reach should narrow to the card's own seat is a question for a card of its own, carried privately to the seat.

N2 (nit) — new. The pin for the row's place compares the source positions of three text anchors. It holds the order and would not notice the block moving inside a later loop or branch. The PR body says why it has no ablation; say the same limit in the pin's title or beside it.

Does the change hold against the code it cites? Yes at this head. The spelling, the join, the fail-closed paths and now the trust statement for the third source each agree with the code, and the template line is bound to the reader again. `listed` remains a consistency reading inside the fleet's trust root and never proof of who rang, which the PR body and the printed key line both still say.
